skills.title: Whiteboard editor
skills.tagline: One raw vertical take in, one finished short out, in the look of Long video to shorts: your face from the first frame, your words in Dynamic text, the pictures sliding out from behind you, white pages that draw the idea, one music, -14 LUFS.

in.title: A raw vertical take
in.says: IT'S NOT YOUR MESSAGE. IT'S YOUR LIST.

what: Hears your take on your Mac, word by word, verbatim (no key needed)
Keeps your take in its own order: the retakes dropped, the dead air cut, graded like your long videos
Opens on your face from the first frame, with the problem as a title above your head and a few pictures of the subject

Puts your words in Dynamic text all along, slides the pictures out from behind you (stock shots as floating screens, GIFs as pinned prints), and sets the idea down on white pages, drawn as a moving schema
One music under the whole short, the sounds of the packs, -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP, the feed's safe zones, checked by measurement
skills.input: A vertical video of you talking to the camera (9:16), e.g. ~/Downloads/take.mp4
skills.output: A finished .mp4 in workspace/videos/, plus the numbers that prove it

style.name: Whiteboard
style.brief: Pipecorn, the look of Long video to shorts on one take: your face from the first frame, Dynamic text, the pictures behind you, white pages that draw the idea
style.line: Your words in Dynamic text, the pictures sliding out from behind you, and white pages that draw the idea as you say it.

drop.title: Drop your take.
drop.lead: A vertical video of you talking to the camera. Claude hears it, cuts the retakes and the dead air, opens on your face with the problem as a title, puts your words on screen, slides the pictures out from behind you, draws the idea on white pages, adds one music and the sounds, then checks it all by measurement.
drop.hint: MP4 or MOV, 9:16, you talking to the camera

skills.title: Short editor

in.title: A raw vertical take
in.says: UH... WAIT. LET ME START AGAIN.

what: Transcribes your take word by word, verbatim, in the language you speak
Assembles a rush with restarts into one clean take (you approve the cut)
Asks once: the music, the pace, and whether you want the old-radio hook bonus
Puts your words as big headlines at the top, passing behind you, with paper plates in stop-motion and your real logos
Sound design from the SFX pack, finished at the platform standard (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP), verified numerically

skills.title: Cold call editor
skills.tagline: One recorded call in, one finished short out: its best line as a glitched hook, the call ringing on paper, then the conversation typed out as it is said.

in.title: A recorded call
in.says: WHERE DID YOU GET MY NUMBER?
flaws: Nothing says it is a call

what: Transcribes the call word by word, verbatim, in the language spoken
Tells the two voices apart by measuring them (a timbre model per voice), then reads the turns
Opens on the call's most suspenseful line, glitched on its stressed words, then places the call on a ringing paper sheet
Types the whole conversation out at the bottom of the frame as it is said, the voice as one thin line of wave
Sound design from the SFX pack and a synthesised ringback tone, finished at the platform standard (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP), verified numerically
skills.input: A vertical video (9:16) whose sound is the call, e.g. ~/Downloads/call.mp4
skills.output: A finished .mp4 in workspace/videos/, plus the numbers that prove it
skills.example: /video-cold-call-editor ~/Downloads/call.mp4, the hook is when she asks where I got her number

style.name: Cold call transcript

skills.title: Scrapbook editor
skills.tagline: One raw take in, one finished short out: every pause cut, your words low and word by word, memes dropped on your face as polaroids, titles handwritten on little notebook scraps with real shadows, the key word in a beautiful serif in your colour, stickers, a red marker drawing as you speak, a music bed and a sound for each thing that lands.
what: Transcribes your take word by word, verbatim, in the language you speak
Cuts every pause, measured on the sound and never into a word: the joins are jump cuts, as in the reference edit
Opens on a title as in the reference: white words, the key word in a beautiful serif in your colour, a handwritten line on paper, stickers popping in around your head

Drops reaction memes on your face as polaroids, always in the same place; writes your titles and your few key phrases by hand on a collage of little notebook scraps that lands, breathes and folds away, a red marker drawing on it, and what you list on stickers; swings each section in; punches the camera on every cut; writes your words low and one by one

A music bed under your voice (Convergence by default), a real paper sound each time a paper lands, the Motionix pack for the stickers, the polaroids and the whooshes, finished at -14 LUFS, verified numerically
skills.input: A vertical video file (9:16) of you talking, e.g. ~/Downloads/take.mp4
skills.output: A finished .mp4 in workspace/videos/, plus the numbers that prove it
skills.example: /video-scrapbook-editor ~/Downloads/take.mp4, my brand colour is #FF5A1F, show my repo on GitHub

skills.title: Explainer editor
skills.tagline: One take of you talking in, one explained short out: you in a frame at the bottom, what you explain drawn above you as you say it, with the motion and the light of an After Effects edit and a sound on everything that moves.

highlights.label: You at the bottom, head out

in.title: A take of you talking
in.says: THERE ARE FIVE THINGS TO GET RIGHT.

what: Transcribes your take word by word, verbatim, in the language you speak
Cuts you out of the picture and sets you in a frame at the bottom of a dark stage lit like a set (a light on each scene, a vignette, dust floating), your head rising out of it

Turns what you say into scenes joined by camera moves (whip pans, rises, push-throughs) and draws each idea on the word that names it: titles, numbered bars, pills, trees, logos, your own screenshots, each with its shadow and its glow, with motion blur and springs, never still
Puts your words between the stage and you, one at a time, and cuts to you full screen with a camera flash a few times a minute

The base skills' sound kit on the big moves (whooshes, a glitch, a riser, the flash) and a light sound on everything that appears (pops, swishes, clicks, shutters, typing: the Motionix pack), each measured as heard, a music bed, finished at -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP and verified numerically
Works from any take: a close one gets a narrower frame, a take of several shots is framed shot by shot; in the dark stage of the reference or its light version
skills.input: A vertical video of you talking to the camera (9:16), e.g. ~/Downloads/take.mp4
skills.output: A finished .mp4 in workspace/videos/, plus the numbers that prove it
skills.example: /video-explainer-editor ~/Downloads/take.mp4, the five steps as a list, my logo when I name the product

style.name: Split explainer

drop.lead: A vertical video of you talking to the camera. Claude cuts you out, sets you in a frame at the bottom, draws what you explain above you as you say it, puts your words on screen one at a time, adds the sound and the music, then checks it all by measurement.
drop.hint: MP4 or MOV, 9:16, you talking to the camera

skills.title: Voice memo to short scripts
skills.tagline: One voice memo in, the short scripts it holds out: three versions of each in the language of your videos, read aloud, two or three feedbacks, the lead magnet in every one.
what: Transcribes your memo word by word, in the language you spoke it
Finds the videos inside it: one point each, 1 to 3 minutes, the big picture and its parts
Writes three versions of each in the language of your videos: Straight, Hook first, and a Story, Contrarian or List
Reads each version aloud with ElevenLabs, so you hear it instead of reading it
Gives two or three feedbacks at most (an idea to add, a big inconsistency, a link to another of your videos) and checks your lead magnet is in every version
skills.input: A voice memo (M4A from Voice Memos, MP3, WAV, or a video)
skills.output: The shorts in workspace/memos/<slug>/memo.json, for the Studio: pick a version, read it on the teleprompter

skills.title: YouTube video editor
skills.tagline: A complete edit of your horizontal YouTube videos, long ones too, in three versions: Facecam + Motion design (you filmed it all, your real voice), Motion design + AI voice (nothing to film), or Facecam + Motion design + AI voice (you film the intro and a few shots, an AI voice says the rest). Real pages, stock shots and GIFs; one music; checked before you see it; the 4K when you say so.
what: Three versions, the same edit: Facecam + Motion design (you filmed the whole video, your real voice), Motion design + AI voice (no filming), or Facecam + Motion design + AI voice (a filmed intro and a few shots, an AI voice for the rest)
Facecam + Motion design: hears your take on your Mac (Whisper, no key), cuts out the retakes, the fillers and the dead air, keeps your real voice all along and your face shots in between
Dresses every face shot: graded, at your speed, you cut out, your words as lockups behind your head, punches, the music from the hook
The two versions with an AI voice: says the script with the voice you pick (an ElevenLabs key), your own cloned once from a take and kept, or a voice of ElevenLabs
Writes from your own words, your idea or your article, with you where it needs a fact: every fact is asked, never invented
Illustrates every sentence in motion design: real homepages and logos, LinkedIn-style cards of made-up people, charts, editorial lines, chapter pages
Adds free stock shots and a few GIFs on their words, credited
Joins it all with one music, renders a 1080p draft and a preview to send, and checks it: -14 LUFS, no black frame, every join; the 4K when you ask
skills.input: Your filmed take (the two Facecam versions), or your script, idea or article (Motion design + AI voice)
skills.output: The video in workspace/videos/ (a 1080p draft and a 720p preview; the 4K on request), and its project in workspace/projects/ to change later

skills.title: Long video to shorts
skills.tagline: Your long video in, several vertical shorts out: its best moments found and put in a new order, the strongest line first as the hook, your real voice, in about 30 s, 1 min and 1 min 30, each ending on a card to the long video if you like.
what: Takes your long video, filmed talking to the camera (16:9 or vertical, derushed or not): the same file the YouTube video editor edits
Hears it once on your Mac, no key needed (or reuses the YouTube video editor's transcript of the same file)
Finds the moments that stand alone, and puts the strongest line first as the hook; each subject in about 30 s, 1 min and 1 min 30
Cuts the retakes and the dead air, at your speed, reframed to 9:16 on your face, graded like the long video
With an ElevenLabs key, says a missing line (a hook, a bridge) in your cloned voice, in your words, never a new fact; without one, only the lines you said
Edits each short in Dynamic text from your first frame, with pictures behind you, white pages that draw the idea, and an end card to your long video on YouTube if you want one
One music, -14 LUFS, checked; the captions for each feed written
skills.input: Your long video, of you talking to the camera, e.g. ~/Movies/my-youtube-video.mp4 (derushed or not)
skills.output: Several finished vertical shorts (1080 × 1920) in workspace/videos/, with their checks and their captions
